FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Road signs convey traffic rules, hazards, location, directions and available services. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
A sign’s color and outline help identify the kind of information it carries. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Warning signs usually have yellow backgrounds and black symbols or lettering, and most are diamond-shaped. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
A warning sign calls for slowing and readiness to stop for the hazard ahead. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A02
Do not race a train to a railroad crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A02
Enter a railroad crossing only when the space beyond can hold your entire vehicle without stopping on the tracks. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A02
Avoid changing gears while on railroad tracks because a stall could leave the vehicle there. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A02
A train can be traveling faster than its large size makes it appear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A02
A circular yellow sign carrying an X and the letters RR warns of a railroad crossing ahead. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
The white railroad crossbuck marks the crossing and requires yielding to trains. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A03
Stop when the alternating lights at a railroad crossing flash for an approaching train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A03
Never go around a lowered railroad-crossing gate. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A03
When a crossing bell or horn sounds, wait until it stops before crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A03
A sign showing multiple railroad tracks warns that more than one train could be crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A03
Check for additional tracks even when no multiple-track sign is present. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A03
School buses, taxis and other for-hire vehicles carrying passengers, and trucks transporting dangerous materials must stop at least fifteen feet before a railroad crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A03
A school-bus driver must open the bus doors before crossing railroad tracks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A03
Work-area signs are generally orange with black lettering or symbols and have a diamond or rectangular shape. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
Work-area warnings can indicate reduced speeds, detours, slow construction equipment, or poor and suddenly changing road surfaces. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
In a work area, a driver must obey a person directing traffic with a flag or sign. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
Regulatory signs communicate requirements for direction, lane choice, turns, speed or parking. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
Regulatory signs may be square, rectangular or specially shaped. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A03
Regulatory signs commonly combine white, red or black backgrounds with black, red, white or green lettering or symbols. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A03
A red circle crossed by a red slash over a symbol forbids the action represented by that symbol. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A03
A speed-limit sign can state a maximum permitted speed or a minimum required speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A03
A posted maximum speed is appropriate only in ideal conditions, and adverse conditions require a lower speed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A02
The round yellow advance railroad warning sign uses black RR letters alongside an X. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A02
A railroad crossbuck is white and X-shaped and bears the words Railroad Crossing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0008]

Misconceptions: the crossbuck requires yielding, while flashing crossing lights require a stop.
Mnemonics: yellow warns, orange marks road work, and the red slash forbids the pictured movement.
Glossary: crossbuck is the white railroad marker; regulatory signs communicate traffic requirements.
Dynamic facts: posted restrictions and active crossing warnings govern the actual location.

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A04
A posted minimum speed requires travel at least that fast to avoid creating a hazard for other drivers. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A04
Choose a different road when its posted minimum speed exceeds the speed you can safely drive. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A04
Lane-control signs show permitted lane movements and turns, often through arrows beside or above the road. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A04
Painted roadway arrows may supplement lane-control signs. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A04
No-passing signs identify places where overtaking is prohibited because sight distance or hidden hazards make it unsafe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A04
Permission to pass never removes the need to check the road and other traffic for safety. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A04
A stop sign is a red octagon bearing white lettering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A04
At a stop sign, stop completely at the stop line if one is present, or at the sign if no line is provided. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A04
After stopping at a stop sign, wait for crossing vehicles and pedestrians to clear, then move only when safe. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A04
A yield sign is a red-and-white triangle with its point facing downward. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A04
At a yield sign, reduce speed and give priority to traffic in the intersection or on the road being entered. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A04
A square sign with a white horizontal bar within a red circle prohibits entry. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A04
Do Not Enter signs can identify an exit ramp or other opening that would lead traffic the wrong way. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A04
A reflective orange triangle on a vehicle’s rear identifies travel below twenty-five miles per hour. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A05
Destination signs usually use green or brown backgrounds with white lettering to identify directions and distances to places. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A05
Service signs use blue backgrounds with white writing or symbols to indicate facilities such as fuel, rest areas or hospitals. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A05
The form and color of a route-number sign identify the type of road. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-R18 | anchor: A05
The handbook recommends choosing a route on a map before travel and following the route signs along the way. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-R19 | anchor: A04
The downward-pointing red-and-white yield sign has red lettering. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-R20 | anchor: A05
Destination signs have a square or rectangular shape. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-R21 | anchor: A05
Service signs have a square or rectangular shape. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec03-R22 | anchor: A05
Route-number signs distinguish interstate, U.S., state, city and county road systems. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-nm-l:new-mexico-motor-vehicle-division-taxati:handbook:pdf-0011]
